rules.title: Review current score before upside
rules.summary: During asset calibration, judge the generated current score from direct or cautiously derived evidence before considering ceiling, future lift, or development potential.
applies_when: A human or agent is labeling current asset value, score ranges, upside, ceiling, or development posture.
The asset has projected future value that could distract from weak current evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The task is explicitly future-roadmap planning and no current score label is being assigned.
A reviewed calibration note already separates current score from ceiling for the asset.
required_actions: Assign or discuss the current score label before using ceiling or upside.
Keep ceiling and lift notes as future-development evidence, not current-score proof.
Record why the current score is about_right, too_high, too_low, or unsure.
rules.danger_if_ignored: Future potential can inflate current scores and make review queues look more mature than the assets actually are.

rules.title: Temp fixture copies are lineage evidence, not independent high-value assets
rules.summary: When a scanned asset is a temp/test fixture copy and canonical/source variants exist, score the specific copy conservatively while preserving its version, coverage, and evolution signal for the asset family.
applies_when: A file is inside a temp, test fixture, copied contract repo, generated fixture, or worktree path.
Same-basename, same-hash, chunk, or normalized-content evidence points to canonical/source variants nearby.
The review is deciding whether the individual copied asset deserves its generated current value score.
does_not_apply_when: The copied fixture is the only available source of truth and no canonical/source variant exists.
The task is specifically evaluating fixture coverage rather than scoring the file as an independent reusable asset.
A reviewed delta proves the temp copy contains a meaningful improvement not present in canonical variants.
required_actions: Classify the path authority first: canonical/source, temp fixture, worktree, archive, or generated copy.
Check whether canonical/source candidates or duplicate variants exist before labeling current score.
If canonical variants exist, treat the temp copy's current score as likely inflated unless the copy has reviewed unique value.
Preserve copy counts, hashes, normalized diffs, and test path lineage as family-level evidence.
Do not delete or ignore differing copies; route meaningful deltas to duplicate/variant review.
rules.danger_if_ignored: A copied fixture flood can create dozens of false high-value assets, while a blanket discard can erase useful version-evolution and coverage evidence.

rules.title: Check semantic evolution separately from copy noise
rules.summary: When reviewing temp copies, near-duplicates, changelogs, deltas, or copied schema families, run or cite deterministic semantic-evolution grading before changing current scores or graph edges.
applies_when: A task is comparing copied files, near-duplicates, schema variants, changelog changes, or deltas over time.
A calibration decision depends on whether differences are real semantic evolution or noise.
Graph edges such as semantic_variant_of, evolved_from, noise_variant_of, or lineage_evidence_for may be created or interpreted.
does_not_apply_when: The task has only one readable asset and no version, duplicate, changelog, or temp-copy evidence.
A reviewed semantic-evolution record already covers the exact family and is cited.
required_actions: Run or cite `asset-dir recommend semantic-evolution` for the relevant family, path class, or schema group.
Separate semantic_change_score from noise_score before labeling current value.
Use the grade registry in `registry/semantic-evolution-grade-registry.json` rather than inventing a grading scale.
Route meaningful evolution to family-level graph edges and keep copied fixture instances from inflating current asset scores.
rules.danger_if_ignored: Agents may either discard valuable version-evolution evidence as fixture noise or over-score noisy copied files as many independent high-value assets.

rules.title: Calculated scores require explicit methodology
rules.summary: Any score, grade, confidence, lift, ceiling, risk, or similarity field that influences review must cite a deterministic formula, inputs, thresholds, uncertainty handling, and methodology version.
applies_when: An agent creates, changes, interprets, or uses a calculated score, grade, confidence label, threshold, lift, ceiling, or risk field.
A calculated value could affect asset ranking, calibration labels, graph edges, review priority, or roadmap evidence.
does_not_apply_when: The task only records raw observations and no calculated value is introduced or used.
The exact methodology version and formula are already cited in the artifact being used.
required_actions: Name the methodology version and cite the registry or document that defines it.
List the inputs, normalization, thresholds, tie-breakers, uncertainty handling, and output range.
Keep current score, ceiling/upside, confidence, semantic-change, and noise scores as separate fields when they mean different things.
If the formula is not defined, mark the field as heuristic or block promotion until the formula is written.
rules.danger_if_ignored: Different agents can assign the same-looking score with different hidden formulas, making calibration, graph edges, and future planning inconsistent or misleading.

rules.title: Capture observable decision traces as bounded lesson candidates
rules.summary: When implementation work reveals a reusable lesson, capture the observable decision trail as candidate learning with applicability limits instead of storing private hidden reasoning or applying the lesson everywhere.
applies_when: A test failure, implementation correction, calibration decision, or user steering creates a reusable lesson for similar future tasks.
The lesson changes when a preflight/midflight rule should surface or how a workflow should be ordered.
does_not_apply_when: The work is a trivial command with no reusable behavior change.
The only available material is private hidden reasoning rather than observable artifacts, commands, edits, failures, or user decisions.
Capturing the lesson would duplicate an already reviewed rule without adding new context.
required_actions: Capture observable artifacts: task trigger, files or commands involved, failure or correction, resulting rule or workflow change, and evidence path.
Record applies_when, does_not_apply_when, and danger_if_misapplied before making it a reusable rule.
Use postflight or a candidate learning file for ordinary lessons; promote to a reviewed preflight rule only when repeated, high-risk, or explicitly human-approved.
rules.danger_if_ignored: Useful implementation learning can disappear, while over-capturing unbounded reasoning can clutter preflight and cause agents to apply lessons outside their safe context.

rules.title: Context-bound lessons need non-applicability and danger notes
rules.summary: Do not reuse a counterfactual lesson unless the agent carries forward where it applies, where it does not apply, and what can go wrong if stripped from context.
applies_when: A lesson, root-cause hypothesis, handoff, or archaeology signal will influence future task order or scoring behavior.
An agent wants to apply a past lesson to a new repo, asset family, calibration batch, or workflow.
does_not_apply_when: The work only stores raw observations and does not derive an action rule.
The lesson has already been reviewed in the same exact context and the review evidence is cited.
required_actions: Carry forward applies_when, does_not_apply_when, and danger_if_misapplied.
State whether the current context matches the lesson's allowed context.
Prefer unsure or human gate when context evidence is weak.
rules.danger_if_ignored: A useful lesson can become harmful when applied as a universal rule outside the conditions that produced it.

rules.title: Software work should search asset-use pay-forward evidence
rules.summary: Before non-trivial software planning or implementation, and again when a hard issue appears, search for prior asset-use feedback that could prevent repeated mistakes or suggest a safer path.
applies_when: An agent is planning or implementing software and the decision, order, dependency, test strategy, or asset choice could affect later work.
An agent encounters a non-trivial issue, repeated failure, failing test, confusing integration, unclear dependency order, or blocker that is not an obvious one-line fix.
An agent can plausibly avoid a future issue by checking prior asset-use feedback, pay-forward guidance, lessons, handoffs, or repo-local learning events before choosing an approach.
does_not_apply_when: The task is a trivial isolated edit, a simple command, or a purely mechanical formatting change with no asset choice or downstream effect.
The agent is only recording raw observations and no planning, implementation, debugging, or issue-avoidance decision is being made.
A reviewed current-context note already cites the relevant asset-use feedback or states that no relevant feedback exists.
required_actions: Search or cite relevant asset-use feedback, pay-forward notes, lessons, handoffs, or repo-local learning events before committing to the plan or when the hard issue appears.
State whether any prior feedback applies, does not apply, or is too weak/noisy for the current context.

If an asset materially influences the work, record before-use expectation when practical and after-use feedback before postflight, including reuse-when, avoid-when, pay-forward guidance, and next-agent actions.
Treat all feedback as candidate evidence; do not let it override source authority, tests, security review, or human gates.
rules.danger_if_ignored: Future agents may rediscover the same failure, choose a poor build order, miss an existing safer asset, or only learn after breaking something that prior pay-forward evidence could have warned them about.

rules.title: Load-bearing decisions need risk-tier review
rules.summary: When a software, repo, roadmap, schema, scoring, governance, dependency, or automation decision can affect many downstream artifacts or future agents, classify the decision as high, medium, or low risk before implementation and run the matching red-team/premortem gate.
applies_when: A planned or active change affects shared contracts, public or repo-local APIs, schemas, registries, ontology, scoring/ranking formulas, roadmap phase gates, CI/hooks, governance rules, source mutation policy, scan scope, dependencies used across modules, or defaults that future agents will inherit.
A decision is hard to reverse, easy to over-trust, likely to influence labels or graph edges, or likely to cascade into other repos, workflows, agents, prompts, tests, or generated evidence.
The agent is writing a roadmap, implementation plan, phase gate, architecture note, or migration path where wrong order or wrong default could create downstream rework.
does_not_apply_when: The change is a small isolated edit with no shared contract, no downstream consumer, no authority boundary, no generated-score effect, and an obvious rollback.
The work only records raw observations or generated candidate evidence without changing behavior, defaults, schemas, gates, or source/repo authority.
A reviewed risk-tier decision already covers the same exact change, context, and downstream scope and is cited.
required_actions: Classify the decision before implementation as high, medium, or low risk using `docs/LOAD_BEARING_DECISION_REVIEW.md`.

For high-risk decisions, stop for human attention, list downstream blast radius, gather at least two plausible options, run an implementer self red-team and premortem, request fresh-eyes review from another AI or reviewer using the template, define rollback and kill criteria, and propose an A/B or bounded comparison when feasible.
For medium-risk decisions, record why the risk is not high, run a short self-premortem, identify tests and rollback, and request fresh-eyes review when uncertainty or downstream ambiguity remains.
For low-risk decisions, state why the change is isolated and reversible, then run normal validation.
Store the risk-tier note, red-team findings, premortem, chosen option, rejected options, validation plan, and remaining unknowns as evidence or in the repo-local learning loop.
rules.danger_if_ignored: A future agent may quietly choose a bad default, schema, scoring formula, source-boundary rule, migration order, or automation hook that multiplies across repos and future agents before a human notices.

rule: Reviewed learning rules are deterministic preflight and midflight routing aids. They constrain agent behavior but do not promote generated observations to source truth.
